subject: Anatomy
content: Anatomy is the study of the structure of the human body, including its parts and organ systems.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The heart is the central pump of the cardiovascular system and works together with blood and blood vessels to support circulation.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: Blood is a component of the cardiovascular system that transports substances such as oxygen, nutrients, and waste products through the body.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: Arteries are blood vessels included in the cardiovascular system and are associated with carrying blood away from the heart.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: Veins are blood vessels that form part of the cardiovascular system and participate in returning blood through the circulation.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The respiratory system includes structures such as the nasal cavity, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, lungs, and pleura.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The bronchi are conducting airways of the respiratory system and are included among the structures listed under the bronchial system.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The lungs are major organs of the respiratory system and are associated with breathing and pulmonary function.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The trachea is one of the major airway structures of the respiratory system and connects the upper airway with the bronchial tree.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The pleura is a structure associated with the lungs and is included in the anatomy of the respiratory system.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The digestive system is a series of organs involved in breaking food down so the body can absorb and use nutrients.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The esophagus is part of the digestive tract and carries swallowed material toward the stomach.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The stomach is a major organ of the digestive tract and receives swallowed food from the esophagus.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The small intestine is part of the digestive tract and is the principal site where nutrients are absorbed from digested food.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The large intestine receives material that remains after passage through the small intestine and is involved in water absorption and elimination of fecal material.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The liver is one of the major organs associated with the digestive system.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The gallbladder is an organ associated with the digestive system and is included among the abdominal digestive organs.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The pancreas is an organ associated with the digestive system and is included among the major digestive organs.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The urinary system includes the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The kidneys are organs of the urinary system that filter wastes and extra water from the blood to produce urine.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The ureters are tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The urinary bladder stores urine until it is released during urination.

subject: Anatomy
content: The skeleton provides structural support for the body.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: Joints are locations where two or more bones come together and allow movement of the skeleton.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: Cartilage is a flexible tissue that covers the ends of bones at many joints and helps provide a smooth joint surface.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: Tendons are strong connective tissues that connect muscles to bones and contribute to joint movement.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: Ligaments connect bones to one another at joints and contribute to joint stability.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: Muscles provide force and strength that enable movement of the body.

content: The brain is a major organ of the nervous system and is involved in functions such as memory, communication, movement, and coordination.
license: Public domain content identified by MedlinePlus

subject: Anatomy
content: The spinal cord is a major structure of the nervous system and is associated with communication between the brain and the rest of the nervous system.

subject: Anatomy
